::: {#def-homogenous-random-network-interference .theorem}
# Homogeneous random network interference

An exposure mapping exhibits homogeneous random network interference with respect to a set of [graph generators](#def-graph-generator)

$$
\mathcal H = \{\boldsymbol \psi : \boldsymbol \psi \subset \mathbf V \text{ is a graph generator} \}
$$

if it is [separable](#def-separability) and all its component functions are [network exposure mappings](#def-network-exposure-mapping) with respect to $\mathcal H$. An NPSEM exhibits homogeneous random network interference if all its exposure mappings do. This is [homogeneous network interference](#def-homogeneous-network-interference) with $\mathcal H$ holding graph generators in place of fixed graphs.
:::
